Functions of Many Variables

We have seen several different forms of the Chain Rule in this section, but each one is just a special case of one general formula. When solving particular problems, it may help to draw the appropriate branch diagram by placing the dependent variable on top, the inter- mediate variables in the middle, and the selected independent variable at the bottom. To find the derivative of the dependent variable with respect to the selected independent vari- able, start at the dependent variable and read down each route of the branch diagram to the independent variable, calculating and multiplying the derivatives along each route. Then add the products found for the different routes.
